subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs VendorX — proposed POC and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmepay.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@acmepay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs VendorX — proposed POC and next steps

Thanks again for the conversation today — good to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Pain points you called out
- Production latency spikes during peak processing windows (p95 frequently > 600ms for average prompts)
- Cost per inference is higher than forecasted; looking to reduce unit costs by ~30–40%
- Embeddings pipeline needs better throughput for a 10k-document index rebuild
- Data governance: strict data residency and KMS/BYOK requirement; audit logs for model inputs/outputs
- Quality: some generation drift on transaction-related prompts (hallucination concern)

Goals for the evaluation
1) Demonstrate consistent p95 latency < 200ms for typical 512-token prompts under realistic concurrency
2) Show cost-per-token reduction via batching/caching while keeping latency SLOs
3) Embeddings throughput for incremental indexing of 10k docs within a 2 hour window
4) Validate security posture: SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, retention controls
5) Compare output quality on 50 representative prompts (measure hallucination/regression)

High-level vendor comparison (from today’s discussion)
- Redwood: unified runtime with prefix/KV caching, model quantization options, private/VPC deployment available, traceable evals and rollouts. We can run dedicated nodes to mirror peak load and provide expert tuning.
- VendorX: lower list price; lacks private deployment and aggressive caching; SLA/observability limited based on what you described.

Proposed bake-off/POC (2 weeks) — tests we recommend
- Latency/load test: reproduce your peak trace (we’ll ask for a 24–48h sample) and measure p50/p95/p99
- Cost test: run a 100k-token baseline workload and estimate normalized cost for 1M tokens with our batching/caching knobs
- Quality/regression: run 50 domain prompts and compare hallucination rates and answer accuracy across models
- Embeddings throughput: incremental indexing test for 10k docs (wall time and CPU/GPU utilization)

Open questions we need answered this week
- Can you share a sanitized 24–48h request trace and representative prompt set?
- Which KMS provider will you require for BYOK?
- Procurement timeline for PO and required contract terms (term length, data residency clause)

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-summary.pdf (POC scope + test matrix)

Next steps
- If that looks good, we’ll: (1) deliver a POC scope + SOW, (2) provision a dedicated test cluster, (3) schedule kickoff (preferably Mon 6/23).
- Please confirm primary success criteria and the procurement contact.

Thanks — I’ll cc our SE (Rishi) to propose the technical test matrix.

Best,
Ben Carter

Hi Sophie — brief technical plan and what we’ll need to run the tests you care about.

POC test matrix (attached: redwood-poc-test-matrix.csv) — summary below:
- Latency/load test: we’ll ask for a 24h request trace (timestamps + prompt lengths + concurrency). We’ll re-play at scaled concurrency on a dedicated 4-GPU pool to capture p50/p95/p99 and memory/KV-use patterns.
- Cost normalization: run controlled baseline (no caching) vs caching/quantized models. We’ll report normalized cost per 1M tokens and expected CPU/GPU hours.
- Quality: we need your 50 canonical prompts + expected outputs (or rubric). We’ll run deterministic seeds across model variants and produce a diff + hallucination report.
- Embeddings throughput: provide a sample subset of documents (we can use sanitized data or synthetic corpus that matches size distribution).

Security/ops notes:
- VPC/private deployment: Redwood supports a private control plane and VPC peering. We can provision a private cluster in your VPC and support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault).
- Audit logs: we can stream request/response audit logs to your logging endpoint; retention is configurable per SOW.

Proposed dates: kickoff Monday 2025-06-23, 2-week window for the tests (20 business days including setup). I’ll lead the test execution with a daily 30-min sync the first week.

Attachments: redwood-poc-test-matrix.csv (test cases & endpoints)

I’ll prepare a short runbook for the replay tooling — Ben, can you share the place to upload trace + prompt set?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
